Method of Attack: Using Windows shortcut files (.LNK) containing obfuscated PowerShell commands to download and execute malware payloads
Execution of PowerShell scripts via Regsvr32.exe command-line utility
Downloading DLL payloads from compromised websites and executing them
Previously used Microsoft Office macros and Visual Basic Script (VBS) code combined with .LNK files
Attack Vector: Phishing campaigns delivering malicious .LNK shortcut files
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious .LNK files with obfuscated PowerShell commands padded with nulls
URLs of several compromised websites used to store PowerShell script payloads
Downloaded PowerShell scripts saved in system’s temporary folder with random names
Execution of DLL payloads via regsvr32.exe
